questions.enonce_markdown:
An auxiliary to trade that enables goods to be available when and where needed is;

*Options as printed:* A) Advertising.   B) Insurance.   C) Transport.   D) Warehousing.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Auxiliaries to trade are services that help the movement of goods from producers to consumers. Warehousing stores goods safely until they are needed, so that consumers can find them at the time they want them (time utility); transport moves goods to the place where they are needed (place utility). Advertising informs buyers and insurance covers risks, so neither makes goods physically available. The wording "when and where needed" fits both transport and warehousing, so the question is ambiguous; the intended answer is warehousing, which keeps stock ready in the right place until customers ask for it.

**Intended answer: D (Warehousing).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which retail trader sells goods to consumers on a door-to-door basis?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A hawker is a small retailer who carries goods from house to house (door-to-door) and sells them directly to consumers. A mobile shop is a vehicle that travels along a route and customers come to it; a road side trader sells from a fixed spot beside the road; "retailer" is the general name for all of them.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the reward to an entrepreneur?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The entrepreneur organises the other factors of production and takes the risk of the business. The reward for this risk-taking is profit. Interest rewards capital, rent rewards land, and dividends are the share of profit paid to shareholders of a company, not the entrepreneur's reward in general.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of change of forms of goods is by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Manufacturing is the type of production in which raw materials or semi-finished goods are changed into a different form to make finished goods (for example cocoa beans into chocolate). Commerce only moves and distributes goods, and direct services do not produce goods at all. "Industry" is a wider word that also includes extraction and construction, so manufacturing is the best answer.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "LTD" at end of a company's name signifies?
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Ltd" stands for "Limited" and is used by a private limited company, whose shares are not offered to the general public. A public limited company ends with "PLC". A corporation (public or private) is a state-created body, which is a different thing.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following retail outlets occupies the largest space?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A hypermarket is a very large self-service store, usually on the edge of a town, with a selling area larger than a supermarket and a huge car park. A supermarket is smaller, a tied shop sells the products of one manufacturer, and chain stores are a group of shops under one owner (each shop is small).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which document provides a summary of transactions at the end of every trading period?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A statement of account is sent by the seller to the buyer, usually at the end of the month. It lists all invoices, credit notes and payments of the period and shows the balance still owed. An invoice covers one single transaction, a pro forma invoice is a quotation-like document sent before the sale, and a bank statement is issued by the bank, not by the trading partner.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
State a restriction on foreign trade that does not generate income;

*Options as printed:* A) Tariffs.   B) Quotas.   C) Embargo.   D) Customs duty.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Tariffs and customs duties are taxes on goods crossing the border, so they bring money to the government. A quota (a limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported) and an embargo (a total ban on trade with a country or on a product) are physical restrictions that collect no tax. Both quotas and embargo can therefore be described as restrictions that do not generate income, so the question has two possible answers; the intended answer is quotas.

**Intended answer: B (Quotas).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Customers who buy in bulk benefit from;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A quantity discount is a reduction in price given to a customer who buys a large quantity of goods at one time. A trade discount is given to traders (retailers) because they buy to resell, and a cash discount is given for quick payment.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used to correct an error of overcharge in an invoice is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
If the seller charged too much on an invoice, the seller sends a credit note, which reduces the amount owed by the buyer. A debit note is used for the opposite error (undercharge). A delivery note and a consignment note accompany goods and do not correct invoices.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation E&OE is printed in which of the following trade documents?
questions.corrige_markdown:
E&OE means "errors and omissions excepted". It is printed at the bottom of an invoice and gives the seller the right to correct any mistake in the invoice later (by a credit note or a debit note). The best-known place where it is printed is the invoice. The same note may also appear on a statement of account, but the standard textbook answer is the invoice.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ---------- is also called "shop of shops".
questions.corrige_markdown:
A department store is a large shop divided into departments (clothes, furniture, food, electrical goods) under one roof, each department being like a separate shop: for this reason it is called the "shop of shops". Multiple shops are branches of one firm in many towns, and mail order businesses sell by post.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A transport mode that is flexible over short distances is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Road transport can go from door to door, on many routes and at any time, so it is the most flexible mode for short distances. Sea, river and air transport are tied to ports, rivers or airports and need other transport for the first and last part of the journey.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cheques that can be cashed by anyone are;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bearer cheque is payable to "bearer" (the person holding it), so any person who presents it can receive the cash. An order cheque must be paid to the named payee or to a person to whom the payee endorses it, and a certified cheque is guaranteed by the bank. A blank cheque is an unsigned or unfilled cheque, which is not a type of cheque for payment.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Current assets less creditors equals;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Working capital = current assets - current liabilities, and the creditors (amounts owed within one year) are the current liabilities. Working capital is the money available to run the day-to-day business. Capital employed is fixed assets plus working capital, and capital owned is the owner's own investment. "Circulating capital" is another name for current assets, not the difference.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An order to an agent to buy goods from a named manufacturer is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
An indent is an order sent by an importer to a buying agent (indent house) abroad. In a closed indent the importer names the manufacturer or supplier from whom the agent must buy; in an open indent the agent is free to choose the supplier. A forwarding agent arranges transport and is not an order.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a cheque transaction identify the payee;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The payee is the person or firm to whom the money on the cheque is to be paid. This person is owed money, so he or she is the creditor. The drawer is the account holder who writes and signs the cheque, and the drawee is the bank that pays it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who pays for loading charges in an FOB price quotation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
FOB means "free on board". The seller's price includes all costs until the goods are loaded on the ship at the port of shipment, including the loading charges. After the goods are on board, the buyer (the importer or consignee) pays freight and insurance.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Direct dealing by-passes;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In direct dealing the producer sells straight to the retailer or to the consumer, so the middleman between producer and retailer, the wholesaler, is cut out. Producers and consumers are the two ends of the chain and cannot be by-passed. The usual textbook answer is wholesalers.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A monetary policy tool used to increase the quantity of money in circulation is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the central bank buys government securities on the open market (open market operation), it pays the sellers and so puts more money into the banks and into circulation. Special deposits remove money from the banks and reduce lending; funding replaces short-term government debt with long-term debt, and moral suasion is only an appeal to banks.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An insurance practice that restores the insured in the original position before the loss occurred is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The principle of indemnity says that the insured must be put back in the same financial position as before the loss, no better and no worse. Proximate cause is the real cause of the loss, insurable interest is the financial interest in the thing insured, and utmost good faith means that both parties must disclose all facts.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are corporate bodies EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A corporate body is a business registered as a legal person separate from its owners. A public company, a private company and a public corporation are all incorporated. A partnership is not incorporated: in law the partners and the business are the same, so a partnership is the exception.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is the most important function of a commercial bank?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The main function of a commercial bank is to accept deposits from customers: these deposits are the funds used for all the other services, such as granting loans and making payments. Without deposits, the bank would have no money to lend. The night safe is only an extra service.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Gross profits expressed as a percentage of sales is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Margin = $\dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{sales}} \times 100$. Mark-up is gross profit expressed as a percentage of the cost of goods sold (not of sales). Rate of turnover is about stock, and net profit is profit after all expenses.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a bank customer uses a single cheque to make several payments it is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a credit transfer (bank giro), the customer gives the bank one cheque together with a list of the persons to be paid, and the bank pays each of them in one operation (for example when paying salaries to many workers). A standing order is an instruction to pay a fixed sum at regular dates, a bank draft is a cheque drawn by the bank on itself, and an overdraft is a borrowing facility.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A risk that may lead to an intentional loss is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Jettison is the deliberate throwing of part of the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship and save the ship and the rest of the cargo in an emergency. The loss is intentional, and it is then shared among the owners of the ship and cargo (general average). The other options are types of insurance cover, not risks.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used when goods are transported by a hired means of transport is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A consignment note is made out by the sender and given to the carrier (road or rail transport company) who is hired to carry the goods; it describes the goods, the sender and the receiver. A delivery note is made out by the seller to go with the goods, an airway bill is specific to air transport and a bill of lading to sea transport.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cost of goods sold divided by average stock is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rate of stock turnover = cost of goods sold / average stock. It shows how many times the stock is sold and replaced during a period. Turnover (alone) means total sales, and margin is a profit percentage.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Savings accounts are opened to;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A savings account encourages people to save small amounts of money and pays interest on the balance. It is mainly opened by small income earners who keep money for the future. Regular and high income earners and civil servants usually also hold current accounts to make payments.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document which stipulate how profits are shared in an incorporated business is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The articles of association set out the internal rules of a company, including how dividends and profits are shared and how meetings are held. The memorandum of association deals with the relationship between the company and the outside world (name, objects, capital). A deed of partnership concerns an unincorporated business, and a prospectus invites the public to buy shares.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An advantage of operating a current account is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A current account holder can be allowed to draw more money than the balance (an overdraft) for a short time. A pass book is used with savings accounts, bank charges paid by the customer are a disadvantage, and a current account normally earns no interest.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A country's visible balance plus her invisible balance is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The visible balance (exports minus imports of goods) added to the invisible balance (exports minus imports of services and income flows) gives the balance of payments on current account. The balance of trade is the visible balance alone, the balancing item corrects statistical errors, and the terms of trade compare export prices with import prices.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Balance of payments on current account.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insurance claims are calculated by;

*Options as printed:* A) Actuaries.   B) Assessors.   C) Adjuster.   D) Broker.
questions.corrige_markdown:
When a claim is made, the insurer sends a loss adjuster (claims adjuster) to investigate the loss and calculate the amount to be paid. An actuary calculates premiums and risks, and a broker only arranges the insurance between the client and the insurer. A loss assessor (assessors) also values claims and may be appointed by the insured, so both options B and C could be defended; the intended answer is adjuster.

**Intended answer: C (Adjuster).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an external source of finance to a business?
questions.corrige_markdown:
External sources of finance come from outside the business, for example the issue of shares, loans and debentures. Retained earnings and plough-back (profits kept in the business) are internal sources, and the past savings of the owner are also internal, since they already belong to the business owner.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document which spells out the exact terms of an insurance contract is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The insurance policy is the written contract that sets out all the terms: what is insured, the sum insured, the premium and the conditions. A cover note is only temporary proof of cover, the proposal form is filled in by the person who wants insurance, and the claim form is used after a loss.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent who guarantees to pay for bad debts is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A del credere agent sells goods for a principal on credit and, for an extra commission, guarantees that customers will pay: if a customer does not pay, the agent pays the principal. The other agents do not take this guarantee.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The relationship between a country's exports and imports is termed;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The balance of trade is the difference between the value of a country's exports and the value of its imports of goods. Favourable and unfavourable balance are the two possible results (exports greater or smaller than imports), not the name of the relationship. The terms of trade compare the price of exports with the price of imports.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document showing particulars of items carried in a ship is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The ship manifest is prepared by the shipping company or the captain and lists all the cargo on board (description, quantities, consignors and consignees). It is shown to customs officers at the port. A bill of lading concerns one consignment and is a receipt and document of title for it, and a shipping note is given to the port to allow the goods to be loaded.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The act of an unplanned buying is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Impulse buying is buying something suddenly, without having planned it before entering the shop, because of attractive display, advertising or a special offer. Bulk-buying is buying in large quantities and self-service is a method of selling.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the cost of goods sold is 3,000,000 CFAF and the selling price is 3,750,000 CFAF, then mark-up equals;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gross profit = selling price - cost of goods sold = $3\,750\,000 - 3\,000\,000 = 750\,000$ CFAF.

Mark-up = $\dfrac{\text{gross profit}}{\text{cost of goods sold}} \times 100 = \dfrac{750\,000}{3\,000\,000} \times 100 = 25\%$.

Trap: dividing by the selling price gives the margin, $750\,000 / 3\,750\,000 \times 100 = 20\%$ (option C).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A carrier that carries more passengers and little cargo on fixed routes is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A liner is a ship that sails on fixed routes and to a fixed timetable. A passenger liner carries mainly passengers and little cargo, while a cargo liner carries mainly goods. Tramp ships have no fixed route or timetable, and coastal liners sail along the coast.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that closing stock is 10,000 CFAF, purchases is 60,000 CFAF, opening stock is 30,000 CFAF and sales is 100,000 CFAF. Gross profit equals;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = $30\,000 + 60\,000 - 10\,000 = 80\,000$ CFAF.

Gross profit = sales - cost of goods sold = $100\,000 - 80\,000 = 20\,000$ CFAF.

Trap: 80,000 CFAF (option C) is the cost of goods sold, not the profit.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A business with both private and public ownership is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A para-statal (mixed enterprise) is a business owned partly by the government and partly by private persons, who share the capital and the management. A public enterprise or public corporation is owned wholly by the state, and a public company is owned by private shareholders who may buy shares freely.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Containerization is advantageous for the transportation of goods for the following reasons EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Containers are sealed, so there is less theft (pilfering); they are stacked efficiently, so many goods fit into a given space, and an empty container can be reused for storage or other purposes. Containers do not need transshipment (unloading and reloading of the goods when changing transport mode): they are moved as a whole from lorry to ship to train. "Requires transshipment" is therefore not an advantage and is the exception.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Maximises quantity of goods in a given space.
Can be put into other uses.

questions.enonce_markdown: Joint advertising carried out by MTN, NEXTTEL and ORANGE is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Generic (collective) advertising is paid for by several firms in the same industry to promote the whole product, here mobile telephone services, and not one brand. Competitive advertising is by one firm against its rivals, persuasive advertising tries to convince buyers to choose a product, and mass advertising is addressed to a very large audience.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a disadvantage of advertising?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Advertising costs money, and the firm adds this cost to the cost of production, which can raise the selling price. Educating customers, creating awareness and increasing sales of the product are advantages.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The practice in which goods sold by description must correspond to the description is best describe by;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a sale of goods law, goods sold by description must correspond to the description given by the seller (an implied condition of the contract); this is the idea of the Sale of Goods Act. A Trade Descriptions law, by contrast, forbids false descriptions as a matter of consumer protection, but the wording of the question follows the Sales of Goods Act. The Food and Drug Act deals with the safety of food and medicines and the Hire Purchase Act with credit sales.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a reason for trade restriction?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Governments restrict trade to stop dumping, to keep out harmful goods, to protect local industries and to correct a balance of payments deficit. They do not restrict trade to reduce their revenue: tariffs and duties actually raise revenue. So option C is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Correct a temporal balance of payments.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT used as a criterion for classifying enterprises?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Enterprises are classified by ownership (private, public, mixed), by output (what they produce: primary, secondary, tertiary) and by size (small, medium, large). Demand is not a criterion for classifying enterprises.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The capital with the least risk in a joint-stock company is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A debenture is a loan to the company, and the holder is a creditor who receives fixed interest whether or not the company makes a profit, and who is paid before shareholders if the company is wound up. Equity and preference shareholders are owners and are paid dividends only from profit, so they take more risk.

**Answer: B.**
